Adeptus Custodes.description: Built around Allarus Custodians and Custodian Wardens as the terminator-weight hammer, supported by Custodian Guard battleline, a Blade Champion, Venatari for mobile secondaries, and a Caladius Grav-Tank for anti-armour reach, this is Shield Host delivering elite bodies into midfield through aggressive positioning rather than transports. The engine is sustained primary scoring via 2+/4++ models that simply refuse to leave objectives, with the Blade Champion's Martial Ka'tah cycling and Allarus teleport threat forcing the opponent to over-commit clearing power to dislodge what is effectively T5-6 infantry with invuln stacks. It punishes mid-range shooting armies and anything relying on AP-1 or AP-2 to clear bodies, since 4++ across the entire roster makes volume fire inefficient and the Caladius handles anything trying to armor-threaten from distance. It cracks open against massed Lethal Hits or AP-3+ concentration — Death Guard Plagueburst Crawlers and Knight Demolisher Cannons bypass the invuln math entirely, and the low model count means losing even two Allarus to a focused melta volley collapses the scoring spine before the army can recover.

Adeptus Mechanicus.description: Built around Sicarian Ruststalkers and Infiltrators delivered in Skorpius Duneriders, backed by Skitarii Marshals and Tech-Priest Manipulus buffing Hastarii Fusiliers, this is a Haloscreed Battle Clade mech-rush that plays much faster than AdMech's reputation suggests. The plan is to advance Duneriders into midfield turn one, disgorge Sicarians into isolated targets for high-AP melee spike damage while Hastarii Fusiliers fire Assault-keyword volleys from the second wave, generating primary through bodies-on-objectives scoring backed by Marshal-ordered activation stacking. The layered profile — Sicarian Infiltrators' 5+ invuln and Ruststalker Phosphoenix-boosted AP on the charge, combined with Manipulus extending Hastarii range — punishes mid-tier T4-5 elite infantry lists that can't tank sustained close-range shooting and melee simultaneously. However, this build folds quickly against anything with AP-2+ volume or reliable anti-tank on turn one, since the Dunerider chassis sits at T6 with minimal invulnerable protection and losing the transports before the Sicarians deploy collapses the entire scoring engine.

Adeptus Mechanicus.description: Built around Kastelan Robots with Cybernetica Datasmith buffing, Skorpius Disintegrators providing mobile fire support, and Onager Dunecrawlers anchoring the backfield, this is a Haloscreed Battle Clade list that blends a durable robot anvil with layered mechanised firepower. The engine is Datasmith-buffed Kastelans cycling between Protector and Conqueror protocols — Dakka Fists on Conqueror shredding infantry while Phosphor Blasters on Protector clear screens — while Disintegrators advance-and-fire into whatever the Dunecrawlers haven't already deleted at range. It punishes static gunlines and slow durable grids by combining the Kastelan brick's T6 3+/5++ with consistent medium-range volume that doesn't need to stand still, grinding primary scoring while the opponent burns resources clearing robots that simply reactivate under Datasmith. It cracks open when fast melee or concentrated AP-3+ Melta hits the Kastelans before the Datasmith can reposition — Knights-style focus fire or a Subterranean Assault deepstrike into the robot brick collapses the entire damage engine in one activation window.

Black Templars.description: Built around Sword Brethren, Castellan, and Marshal character stacks delivered behind Repulsor Executioner fire support, this is Righteous Crusaders playing a hybrid tempo game — elite infantry pressure backed by a T8 heavy tank that clears the path forward. The engine is using Assault Intercessors and Sword Brethren to contest midfield objectives while the Repulsor Executioner's Macro Plasma Incinerator and Onslaught Gatling Cannon strip whatever was holding them, with Scout screens denying early deep strike angles. It punishes slower, lower-activation armies that can't match the combined arms threat density — static gunlines in particular struggle to prioritize between the incoming infantry wave and the AP-3 vehicle bearing down on their key units. Where it breaks is against dedicated mobile anti-armour or fast kiting lists that can isolate and delete the Repulsor Executioner before the melee hammers arrive, unraveling the fire-support-plus-assault synergy the list depends on.

Chaos Daemons.description: Built around Great Unclean One as the armored anchor, Poxbringer and Sloppity Bilepiper stacking Disgustingly Resilient buffs into Plaguebearer blobs and Beasts of Nurgle as mid-board enforcers, this is the Plague Legion operating as a layered-defense attrition engine. The win condition is planting 20-30 Plaguebearers on mid-table objectives turn 1 — T4 with a 5+ FNP equivalent and Nurgling screen absorbing chip damage — while the Great Unclean One and Beasts of Nurgle generate a secondary threat that punishes any unit that over-commits to clearing the blob. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Mass Volume Horde lists that rely on Blast templates and volume fire, because Disgustingly Resilient degrades the math on every wound roll while Nurglings deny deepstrike lanes and the Bilepiper's aura keeps the blob combat-effective through attrition. It cracks open against Mobile Anti-Armour lists — Knights and Mont'ka Crisis Suits bring concentrated AP-3+ Melta that cuts through T4 FNP stacks efficiently — and fast skimmer lists that kite the Great Unclean One out of relevance while chipping the slow-moving Plaguebearer scoring units off objectives at range.

Chaos Space Marines.description: Built around Chosen delivered by Chaos Rhinos, Raptors and Warp Talons as fast-flanking threat vectors, and Huron Blackheart's Masters of the Maelstrom detachment providing the strategic scaffolding, this is Huron's Marauders playing a board-control attrition game rather than a pure alpha-strike list. The plan is to flood midfield with Rhino-borne Chosen generating consistent primary scoring while Raptors and Warp Talons chase down lone characters and exposed scoring units, using Huron's free Stratagem economy to stack pressure across multiple fronts simultaneously. It punishes slower positional lists — tank companies and infantry blobs that can't contest multiple threat vectors at once — because the activation spread across transport infantry, jump-pack flankers, and a free-Strat engine is more than static gunlines can track. It struggles against lists that can out-range the Rhino-rush delivery before turn 2 and collapse the Chosen's damage spike, particularly Heavy Gunline builds that pop the transports on turn 1 and strand the melee hammers in the open.

Chaos Space Marines.description: Built around Vashtorr the Arkifane leading a daemon engine stable of Venomcrawlers, Defilers, and Forgefiends, this is the Soulforged Warpack in its most vehicle-dense expression — a mechanised threat wall backed by Warpsmith repair support and a Cultist Mob screen. The engine is Vashtorr's Dark Pact buffs amplifying daemon engine shooting and melee simultaneously: Forgefiends spike anti-armour output at range while Venomcrawlers and Defilers close into melee, with the Warpsmith keeping damaged chassis alive past the point opponents expect. It punishes static gunlines and light-vehicle lists that lack the AP-3+ volume to efficiently strip T9-10 daemon engine hulls before Warpsmith repairs stack, and the Cultist screen soaks deepstrike threats that would otherwise isolate individual engines. The list cracks open when concentrated Melta or Knight-tier Demolisher fire focuses one chassis per turn faster than Vashtorr's repair economy can answer, and mobile anti-armour lists with 12"+ movement can dictate range and isolate engines before the wall coheres.

Drukhari.description: Built around Lelith Hesperax leading Wyches in Raiders and Venoms, with Reavers screening, Incubi as the elite hammer, and a Succubus threading Combat Drug buffs across the Wych Cult core, this is a Spectacle of Spite shell using transport-delivered melee volume rather than the Reaper's Wager shooting hybrid. The win condition is Pain Token accumulation through chip-damage skirmishing followed by a mid-game melee surge — Raiders and Venoms fire-and-fade to farm tokens while Lelith's unit picks an isolated threat to obliterate, then the Reaver screen locks secondaries via Engage on All Fronts and Behind Enemy Lines. It punishes slow durable-grind lists and infantry-heavy positional armies that can't kite away from a 14"-move Raider delivery, with Lelith's 4+ invuln and Wych Combat Drug cycling making the melee core surprisingly hard to one-shot clear. Fast AP-3+ anti-vehicle lists like Mont'ka Crisis Suits or Infernal Lance Knights crack it open by popping the Raider/Venom chassis before disembarkation, stranding the foot-melee units in the open where their 6+ armor becomes a liability.

unitFrequency.datasheet: daemon prince of slaanesh with wings

Emperor's Children.description: Built around Infractors and Flawless Blades delivered in Chaos Rhinos, buffed by a Lord Exultant and a winged Daemon Prince of Slaanesh, this is the Carnival of Excess expression of the Emperor's Children transport-rush game — fast, melee-pointed, and crit-hungry. The engine is Rhino-disembark into close-range Infractor shooting followed by a Flawless Blades counter-charge, with the Lord Exultant's aura stacking Devastating Wounds procs onto an already lethal crit-spike turn while Noise Marines hold backfield objectives and the Daemon Prince hunts isolated targets. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation vehicle lists that can't clear the Rhino wave before the disembark payoff lands — the sheer number of separate threat vectors across infantry hammers, flying characters, and Noise Marine fire forces priority errors. Deep-strike denial screens and high-volume AP-2 shooting crack it open, since popping transports before the disembark collapses the delivery plan and the list lacks the raw body-count to recover primary scoring on foot.

Genestealer Cult.description: Built around Purestrain Genestealers and Acolyte Hybrids flooding forward on foot, screened by Neophyte blob squads and harassed from the flanks by Achilles Ridgerunners and Atalan Jackals, this is the Biosanctic Broodsurge expression of GSC — maximum bodies, maximum cult-symbol threat density. The win condition is OC dominance through sheer model volume: Neophyte screens lock primaries while Purestrains and Hand Flamer Acolytes deliver melee spikes from infiltrate or deep strike, with Reductus Saboteur demolition charges softening anything that tries to hold the line. It punishes Heavy Gunline and static anti-armour lists that can't clear 60+ wounds of mid-board presence before the Genestealers arrive — the activation gap and OC saturation simply outscores them. It struggles against fast mobile lists that kite the foot-speed of the cult and against concentrated blast-template firepower that can clear Neophyte blobs before the Purestrains close the distance.

Genestealer Cult.description: Built around Aberrants, the Abominant, and Purestrain Genestealers supported by Biophagus-buffed Acolyte Hybrids with hand flamers, Biosanctic Broodsurge is a dense melee-horde that floods the board with T5 bodies carrying layered durability through Biophagus Feel No Pain stacks and the Abominant's damage reduction aura. The engine scores primary through sheer OC volume — enough Aberrant and Purestrain models on every objective that the opponent needs dedicated blast-template firepower to dent the claim, while Acolyte flamers and Ridgerunner harassment chip secondary scoring on the flanks. It punishes static gunlines and transport-infantry lists that can't generate enough blast-template activations to clear T5 multi-wound models with FNP, and the Abominant's aura effectively shuts off the alpha-strike turns that Land-Raider Possessed builds rely on. However, dedicated Russ Demolisher companies and Knight Gatling-Cannon lists run the activation efficiency to delete the wound pool before the horde closes, and Drukhari skimmer fire denies the engagement entirely by kiting outside charge range while chipping the Ridgerunners off the board.

Grey Knights.description: Built around Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight and multiple Nemesis Dreadknight chassis supported by Castellan Crowe's Purifier bubble, Brotherhood Librarian psychic buffs, and Interceptors for secondary coverage, this is a Sanctic Spearhead expression that marries T7 monstrous walkers with a layered mid-board toolbox. The plan is to push the GMNDK and NDK pair into the opponent's primary scoring zone by turn 2, using Crowe's Purifier synergies to stack Lethal Hits via Grey Knights' psychic enhancement strats while Interceptors teleport-farm secondaries on the flanks. The 4+ invuln on NDK chassis combined with Brotherhood Librarian defensive casts absorbs most alpha-strike output from mid-tier shooting lists, and the GMNDK's Titanic profile bullies anything short of dedicated anti-armour out of midfield objectives. However, concentrated AP-3+ Melta from Mobile Anti-Armour lists and stacked FNP bricks like Pactbound Zealots Possessed in Land Raiders can crack the chassis before the Purifier Lethal combo pays off, leaving the list stranded on primary with no fallback scoring engine.

The engine is locking Paladins onto midfield objectives behind a 2+/4++ wall while Interceptors use their Teleport Shunt to harass scoring units and deny secondary plays, grinding primary from turn 2 onward. That layered durability — 2+ armor on Terminators stacked with 4+ invulns and Voldus's psychic support — punishes low-AP shooting lists and mobile skirmish fires that can't shift T4 bodies with meaningful volume. The crack is concentrated AP-3+ with high damage output: Knight Melta, Chaos Knight Gatling Cannons, or Mont'ka Battlesuits can strip the Terminator wall faster than Voldus can cycle psychic buffs, leaving the scoring engine stalled with no cheap bodies to plug the gaps.

Imperial Knights.description: Built around six-plus Armigers — Helverins for long-range autocannon suppression and Warglaives for melee threat — anchored by a Knight Warden or Paladin as the points-sink hammer and a Callidus Assassin for character sniping, this is a Skyreaper Lance activation-spam list wearing 4+ ion-shield invulnerable saves on every chassis. The plan is to flood the board with T8 platforms that each demand a dedicated answer, scoring primary through sheer OC saturation while Helverin autocannons strip light vehicles and Warglaives threaten melee on anything exposed. It punishes low-activation anti-armour lists — Knights or T'au Mont'ka that concentrate fire can't kill eight targets before running out of shooting phases, and the Callidus deletes the buff character that makes those lists function. Massed Melta or AP-3 volume from a true big-Knight gunline concentrates enough damage to pop Armigers faster than the activation count protects them, and infantry-heavy horde lists simply out-OC the swarm on objectives once the Warglaives are bogged in tarpit melee.

Imperial Knights.description: Built around a Knight Castellan anchor supported by Knight Destriers, Errants, and Gallants — with Inquisitorial Agents rounding out the roster — this is an Questor Allegiant-style mixed-lance list that leans hard into the Castellan's plasma decimator and volcano lance as its primary damage engine. The plan is to use the Castellan's 36"+ range to delete priority targets early while the faster Destrier and Gallant chassis close mid-board and lock opposing hammers in melee, with the Inquisitorial splash providing secondary-scoring reach and screen-denial the pure Knights roster can't manage alone. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists hardest — the Castellan's AP-3+ volcano lance cracks T9 Russes on 3+ to wound while the melee Knights absorb the return fire on 4+ ion-shield invulns, and the activation advantage over a 4-6 Russ company lets the Knights dictate primary scoring tempo. Fast mobile lists running massed Melta — Mont'ka Crisis Battlesuits or Infernal Lance Wardogs — can strip the Castellan before it fires twice, and mob tarpits like War Horde's 30-Boyz advance lock the melee Knights in place while the Castellan's long-range firepower becomes irrelevant inside 6".

Imperial Knights.description: Built around Cerastus Knight Atrapos and Cerastus Knight Lancer alongside Canis Rex, this is a Freeblade Lance-style mobile elite list that leans on the Cerastus chassis's 14" move and native 4+ invuln to close aggressively while maintaining genuine anti-armor bite from the Atrapos's Atrapos Lascutter and Conversion Beam Cannon at AP-3 to AP-4. The plan is to use superior speed to isolate and delete priority targets — Knights Errant, heavy vehicles, tough-saves units — turn by turn while Armiger Warglaives screen and contest secondaries, letting the list outscore on primary through OC dominance rather than tabling. The Cerastus chassis punishes static planted gunlines (AM Grizzled Company, Devastator-station Marines) hard, since 14" movement breaks firing-arc management and the Atrapos's Lethal Hits trigger cracks T7-9 efficiently without needing Melta range. Mob tarpits and activation-heavy Transport Infantry lists crack this open — War Horde or Pactbound Zealots with Cultist screens have enough bodies to lock the Knights in melee or flood objectives the three-to-five activation list simply can't contest across the full table.

unitFrequency.datasheet: ironkin steeljacks with heavy volkanite disintegrators

Leagues of Votann.description: Built around Brôkhyr Thunderkyn, Einhyr Hearthguard, and a Hekaton Land Fortress anchor, this is the Mercenary Oathband's answer to the mid-table brawl — a compact, mid-T elite gunline that advances and fires rather than kiting or castling. The engine is straightforward: Hernkyn Pioneers provide scout coverage and secondary reach while Thunderkyn and Ironkin Steeljacks concentrate AP-2 to AP-3 volkanite fire onto priority targets, with the Hekaton soaking return fire at T10 and threatening melee if the opponent over-commits forward. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count vehicle lists that can't match its blend of mid-range firepower density and T5-6 wound stacking — Thunderkyn's Heavy Volkanite Disintegrators shred T6-8 chassis that expect to trade efficiently on HP. It struggles against mass-horde activations and fast melee delivery, specifically Transport Infantry lists that can screen the mid-table and force the Votann brick to absorb a counter-punch it can't fully weather at the depth of its invulnerable save coverage.

Leagues of Votann.description: Built around Cthonian Beserks delivered by Sagitaurs alongside Berehk Stornbröw and Buri Aegnirssen, this is Mercenary Oathband running a War Horde-style mobile brawler with a Votann twist: elite T5 melee hammers in fast transports backed by Einhyr Hearthguard as the durable mid-board anchor and Hernkyn Pioneers harassing flanks. The plan is to disgorge Beserks into the opponent's scoring units by turn 2 while Berehk's buff stack amplifies the charge — trading favorably on primary through sheer melee throughput rather than objective camping. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation vehicle lists hard, because the Sagitaur delivery bypasses screen layers and the Beserks' T5 volume-attack profile eats elite infantry that can't clear them before the counter-score lands. Fast kiting lists and layered invuln armies crack it open — Drukhari fire-and-fade denies the charge window entirely, and 2+/4++ platforms like Custodes absorb the Beserk swing without yielding the trade.

Necrons.description: Built around walls of Canoptek Wraiths screened by Scarab Swarms and anchored by a Technomancer, this is Awakened Dynasty at its most oppressive — a C'tan-stuffed toolbox that pairs the Nightbringer, Void Dragon, and Deceiver as independent damage-dealing engines behind an unkillable melee vanguard. The engine is mid-board control: Wraiths with 4+ invulnerable saves and Technomancer's reanimation support plant on objectives while C'tan shards apply concentrated AP-3+ and mortal-wound pressure to whatever the opponent commits to clear them, scoring primary through attrition rather than burst. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and static shooting armies hard — Wraiths close the distance before Russ firing arcs can reduce them below critical mass, and C'tan shards are effectively immune to Blast templates. Layered defenses crumble it: Death Guard Vectorium's Disgustingly Resilient stacks plus Contagion debuffs drag the Wraiths below their damage threshold turn by turn, and anything with massed AP-3 Melta or concentrated Lethal Hits volume — Mont'ka Battlesuits, Knight Demolisher cannons — can crack the C'tan before their mortal output pays off.

The engine works by killing or halving a unit with Destroyers each turn to proc Cursed Legion's army-wide +2 Strength buff, then cycling Ophydians and Tomb Blades onto contested objectives while the Lokhusts dictate trades from range. Necrons.description: Built around Doomsday Arks as the primary damage engine, supported by the Silent King's command aura and Lychguard bodyguard bricks, this is the Starshatter Arsenal gunline in its most committed form — long-range S14 AP-3 Doomsday Cannons backed by Tomb Blades for objective harassment and Flayed Ones threatening flanks from reserve. The plan is to delete high-value targets at range each turn using concentrated Doomsday Cannon fire (D6+6 damage per shot against T9+ chassis), while the Silent King's Triarch protocols and Lychguard's 4+ invuln wall hold the midline and Reanimation Protocols grind down opposing attrition. It punishes static gunlines and durable-saves armies that can't match the raw AP-3 volume — T7-9 chassis and multi-wound elite infantry dissolve under focused Doomsday Ark fire while Lychguard absorb the counter-push with their dispersion shields. Aggressive mobile lists with fast melee delivery — Berzerker Warband Rhino rushes, Subterranean Assault deepstrikes — crack it open by closing 24" before the Arks can pivot, since the chassis has zero fall-back shooting and the Flayed One screens can only delay rather than stop a committed turn-1 melee threat.

Orks.description: Built around towering Boyz mobs led by Ghazghkull, Warbosses, Big Bosses, and Painboys, with Stormboyz and a Weirdboy rounding out the support bench, this is War Horde at its most straightforward — a wall of T5 green bodies backed by every character buff the Ork codex offers. The win condition is total OC dominance: plant 30-Boyz blobs on every mid-board objective turn 1, keep them alive through Painboy Feel No Pain and Warboss re-rolls, and outscore the opponent on primary while Stormboyz deliver a second-wave counter-punch into anything that tries to contest. Sustained Hits 1 on every melee weapon means even base Slugga Boyz threaten to mulch elite infantry off an objective, and the character stack — Ghaz plus two or three Bosses plus Painboy — makes each mob punishingly hard to clear without dedicating an entire army's shooting to the task. Fast shooty lists that stay outside charge range and chip wounds faster than the Painboy can patch them are the natural counter, since Drukhari-style fire-and-fade and Aeldari Dark Reapers with Lethal Hits can bleed the mobs down before they ever swing.

Orks.description: Built around Big Meks with Shokk Attack Guns, Lootas, Tankbustas, and Flash Gitz, this is a More Dakka-flavored Ork shooting list that leans hard on massed volume fire rather than the melee mob that defines War Horde. The plan is to flood the board with cheap Boyz blobs holding objectives while the shooting battery — Shokk Attack Guns threatening random mortal-wound spikes, Lootas cycling Dakka Dakka Dakka procs, and Tankbustas lighting up vehicles — grinds the opponent's scoring units off the table from range. It punishes low-activation gunlines and castle lists that can't clear a 30-Boyz screen fast enough to reach the fire base before the mortal-wound accumulation tips the trade, and the sheer body count out-OCs anything relying on elite objective holders. The core weakness is that neither the shooting nor the mob density reaches the ceiling of the specialists: Dark Reaper Lethal Hits ignore the screen entirely, fast skimmer lists kite outside Shokk Attack Gun threat range, and without War Horde's Sustained Hits 1 blanket, the melee counter-punch is underpowered when the opponent commits to clearing the guns.

Orks.description: Built around Squighog Boyz, Beast Snagga Boyz, the Beastboss on Squigosaur, and Mozrog Skragbad delivering T5-6 bodies in enormous numbers, this is Da Big Hunt operating at full Beast Snagga purity — every unit in the roster qualifies for the detachment's anti-vehicle buffs and charge-bonus strats. The engine is a two-wave surf: Beast Snagga Boyz blob onto mid-board objectives turn 1 with Sustained Hits 1 backing every melee swing, while the Squigosaur characters and Squighog Boyz punch through T9-11 chassis with Devastating Wounds volume to deny the opponent's own anchor units. It punishes low-activation vehicle lists like Infernal Lance and Questoris Companions brutally — five Knight activations can't clear enough Beast Snagga bodies per turn to stop primary bleeding, and the Squighog charge windows arrive before Knights can re-angle firing arcs. Heavy infantry gunlines like Grizzled Company are the crack point, as Demolisher Cannon blast templates clear Beast Snagga Boyz faster than FNP or Sustained Hits can compensate.

Space Marines (Astartes).description: Built around Vulkan He'stan and Adrax Agatone doubling down on Infernus Squads and Eradicators inside Land Raider Redeemers, this is a Firestorm Assault Force-style mech list that weaponises the Salamanders Promethean doctrine — stacking re-rolls on Melta and Flame weapons across every activation. The engine is transport delivery: Redeemers disgorge Infernus Squads at melta range while Eradicators provide the long-gun backstop, letting the list spike damage on priority targets while scoring primary through transport OC and post-disembark battleline presence. Against static infantry blobs and T5-6 mid-board brawlers, concentrated Melta at half-range with full re-rolls from He'stan tears through toughness brackets that would otherwise demand multiple turns of chip damage. Fast mobile lists and skimmer kite-fests crack it open — once the Redeemers are stripped and Infernus Squads are on foot, the 10"-move infantry can't chase a 14"+ Raider chassis to re-engage.

unitFrequency.datasheet: marneus calgar in armour of antilochus

Space Marines (Astartes).description: Built around Marneus Calgar's Command re-roll aura buffing a firebase of Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts, with Victrix Honour Guard bodyguarding him and Scout and Incursor screens pushing forward for objective pressure, this reads as an Anvil Siege Force or Ironstorm Spearhead heavy-gunline castle with mobile forward elements. The engine is Calgar's aura sustaining consistent AP-2/AP-3 output from the Repulsor Executioner's macro-cannon and the Ballistus's twin lascannons while the screens deny deepstrike approaches and the Victrix bubble keeps Calgar alive to keep generating Command re-rolls. It punishes planted gunlines and transport-infantry lists hardest — the volume of S14/S10 shooting deletes Rhinos and Russes before they can dictate the trade, and Scout screens close off the deepstrike windows that would otherwise flank the castle. Aggressive mobile lists running melee-delivery transports or fast cavalry that can ignore the screen and crash directly into the firebase expose the build's lack of melee staying power once Victrix models are traded away.

Space Marines (Astartes).description: Built around Techmarines babysitting a battery of Redemptor and Brutalis Dreadnoughts, backed by Hellblasters and Intercessors holding the midline, this is an Anvil Siege Force or Ironstorm Spearhead expression that plants heavy chassis in firing lanes and grinds opponents down with sustained AP-2/AP-3 volume. The engine is Techmarine repairs keeping Redemptors at full Damage bracket while Hellblasters (S8 AP-4 D3) and Redemptor macro plasma cannons stack high-AP shots into elite targets each turn, with Infiltrators deployed forward to deny deepstrike and screen the gun battery. It punishes slow durable lists — Plague Marines and T9 vehicles can't close the gap before Redemptor onslaught and Hellblaster overcharge chew through their wound pools — and the Brutalis provides a melee deterrent that stops anything that does close from freely wrecking the backline. Fast kiting lists and mobile anti-armour are the hard counters: a 14"-move Raider or a Knight Despoiler closing to Melta range can dictate the engagement on their terms, and Dreadnoughts with 8" base movement can't reposition quickly enough to deny the charge or escape the firing arc.

Space Marines (Astartes).description: Built around Terminator Assault Squads, Terminator Squads, and a Librarian in Terminator Armour anchored by Caanok Var, this is a 1st Company Task Force-style brick that delivers massed Terminator bodies via Land Raider or deep strike into the opponent's scoring spine. The engine is Psychic-buffed Terminator hammers crashing into midfield objectives on turn 2, holding them under a wall of 2+/5++ bodies while the Librarian's force multiplication and the Ancient's re-roll aura sustain the trade over multiple turns. It punishes heavy gunlines and transport infantry hard — 2+ armor ignores most Russ-tier AP-2 shooting and the Terminator footprint simply out-OCs Rhino-delivered squads that can't crack T5 multi-wound models efficiently. Fast mobile anti-armor and skimmer kite lists crack it open by staying outside engagement range and farming wounds through sustained AP-3+ or melta fire that bypasses the 2+ entirely.

Space Marines (Astartes).description: Built around a squadron of Land Speeders and Storm Speeder Hammerstrikes and Thunderstrikes backed by Vindicator siege tanks, this is an Ironstorm Spearhead-style fast gunline that floods the table with mobile heavy-weapon platforms rather than infantry delivery. It scores by dictating range — Hammerstrikes put Multi-Melta and Krakstorm Missile volume onto T7-9 chassis at 24" or less while Thunderstrikes handle elite-infantry clearing, and the Vindicator's S14 AP-3 Demolisher Cannon punishes anything that tries to anchor mid-board; Incursors and Outriders screen the flanks and contest objectives cheaply enough that the shooting never has to stop. It punishes planted gunlines and low-mobility armies hard — the 16"-move Speeder chassis denies Russ or Devastator firing arcs by repositioning every turn, and the anti-armour concentration overwhelms heavy tanks before they can spread damage across the skimmer stack. Mob tarpits and high-activation infantry hordes crack it open, because the list's activation count is too thin to contest primaries under sustained body-count pressure while also committing its shooting budget to keeping the Speeders alive.

Space Wolves.description: Built around Thunderwolf Cavalry as the primary hammer, Wulfen with Storm Shields as the durable mid-board anvil, and Wolf Guard Terminators as the elite close-support, this is Wolf Jail — the Stormlance Task Force expression that uses Scout Squads and Intercessors as cheap objective-holders freeing the cavalry to hunt. The engine runs a classic bait-and-charge cycle: Scouts and Intercessors claim and screen early objectives while the Thunderwolves threaten every midfield angle, forcing the opponent into unfavorable positioning before the Wulfen and Terminators crash in on turn 2-3 to clean up exposed units. At a modest 52.9% win rate this is a generalist list that punishes slow positional armies — static gunlines and infantry hordes that can't reposition away from T5 Thunderwolves with 3+/5++ charging across 16"+ threat ranges — but the multi-axis spread across nearly every playbook signals a lack of spiked identity. Fast kiting lists (Drukhari Raiders, Aeldari Aspect Host) and crit-stacking Transport Infantry like Pactbound Zealots crack it open by either staying permanently outside the charge envelope or absorbing the Thunderwolf punch with Cultist screens and returning Devastating Wounds fire before the Wulfen can consolidate.

T'au Empire.description: Built around Riptide Battlesuits and Broadside Battlesuits as the heavy-firepower spine, with Piranhas and Stealth Battlesuits providing the forward harassment screen and Pathfinders delivering Markerlights to lock down targets, this is a Mont'ka-pattern gunline that uses speed as its defensive layer. The engine is concentrated AP-3+ and Melta-equivalent fire funneled through Markerlight-buffed firing solutions — Broadsides spike anti-tank output at range while Riptides cycle targets via Heavy Burst Cannon or Ion Accelerator profiles, and Piranhas Jump-Shoot-Jump to deny counter-engagement. It punishes static heavy gunlines and transport-delivered infantry hard, matching or exceeding their threat range while denying the firing arcs that Russ tanks and Rhino-rush lists depend on to dictate trade sequences. What cracks it open is the same speed-versus-speed problem that defines T'au: fast melee-threat lists like Cursed Legion Necrons or Berzerker Warband close the JSJ gap before the Riptides can reposition, and once anything locks a Battlesuit in melee, the entire damage engine stalls.

T'au Empire.description: Built around Commander Farsight and a dense stack of Crisis Battlesuits — Coldstar, Enforcer, Sunforge, Fireknife, and Starscythe variants — this is Mont'ka in its purest expression: four or five independent battlesuit blocks that Jump-Shoot-Jump out of return fire every single turn. The win condition is sequential target elimination through Crisis Suit stacking; Sunforge Crisis bring concentrated Melta within 12" on AP-3+ for hard targets, while Fireknife and Starscythe variants clean up mid-toughness units, all scoring primary through sheer board presence as the opponent runs out of answers across multiple threat vectors simultaneously. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and static mid-board brawlers severely — planted Russ chassis and T5-6 mobs can't dictate the engagement range against a list that repositions every activation, and AP-3+ Melta ignores the T9 armor saves that slow durable lists rely on. However, against Mobile Toolbox lists with fast melee delivery — Wraith bricks, Khornate elites in Rhinos, Subterranean Assault deepstrikes — the JSJ safety net collapses once a charge connects, and Crisis Suits without melee output evaporate when locked.

Thousand Sons.description: Built around Rubric Marines and Scarab Occult Terminators stacked with Sorcerers in Terminator Armour, Exalted Sorcerers, and Tzaangor bodies in volume, this is a Warpforged Cabal that plays as a mass-infantry control list with genuinely layered defenses rather than a classic psychic-alpha build. The engine is occupying midfield with large Rubric and Tzaangor blobs — their All Is Dust 2+ armor save against AP0/AP-1 effectively functions as a FNP-equivalent defensive layer — while Scarab Occult Terminators and character-stacked Sorcerers deliver Lethal Hits and Warpflame mortal wound procs onto whatever the opponent commits to clearing the screen. It punishes heavy gunline and transport-delivery lists hard, because the 2+ save on Rubrics eats Russ Battle Cannon and Rhino-disgorged Possessed alike without the AP-3 volume needed to clear them efficiently at scale. The critical vulnerability is concentrated AP-3+ or Melta fire — the Rubric durability collapses entirely the moment the opponent fields enough weapons that bypass All Is Dust, and at 46% this build is fighting the current meta's prevalence of exactly that weapon profile in Knights and Mont'ka Battlesuits.

Thousand Sons.description: Built around Sekhetar Robots screening for a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings and Defiler/Forgefiend daemon-engine support, with Tzaangor Enlightened and a Tzaangor Shaman providing layered utility, this is a Hexwarp Thrallband-style construct-and-caster control shell wearing surprisingly aggressive daemon-engine teeth. The engine is Lethal Hits volume from the Robots and Forgefiend's autocannons softening key targets while the Daemon Prince and Defiler spike priority pieces, all backed by the Shaman's psychic support cycling buffs that keep the Robots alive through AP-2 fire longer than the opponent expects. Its distributed threat profile — daemon engines threatening armor at range, Enlightened denying screens, Robots holding midfield on 4+ invuln-equivalent durability — punishes static gunline matchups and slow durable-grind lists that can't redirect fast enough to address three distinct pressure vectors simultaneously. What cracks it open is concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour focus fire: the daemon engines are T7-8 but lack true 4++ saves, so a Mont'ka Crisis-suit alpha or Knight Despoiler Gatling salvo that collapses the Defiler or Forgefiend in turn 1 strips the anti-armor backbone before the Robots can anchor the midfield trade.

Tyranids.description: Built around the Norn Assimilator as its mobile murder-anchor, supported by Psychophage, Haruspex, and Pyrovores as mid-board enforcers, with Ripper Swarms and Tyrant Guard completing the layered threat package, this is Assimilation Swarm running its canonical consumer-engine gameplan. The list drives a wall of T9-10 Monsters into mid-table turn 1, using the Norn Assimilator's Synapse bubble and Tyrant Guard screening to absorb the alpha strike while Pyrovore flame templates and Psychophage mortal-wound auras grind opposing infantry off objectives, scoring primary through sheer presence and attrition rather than finesse. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Transport Infantry lists hard — Russes and Rhinos can't clear T9+ Monsters efficiently enough to stop the scoring tide, and the Haruspex's Devastating Wounds melee profile cracks open light vehicles that try to screen. Its core vulnerability is fast kiting lists and concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour fire: Drukhari skimmers deny the engagement entirely, and Knight Melta concentrating onto the Norn Assimilator removes the Synapse anchor that holds the whole engine together.

Tyranids.description: Built around the Norn Emissary and Norn Assimilator as the dual T9+ melee-and-shooting hammers, supported by a Maleceptor for psychic pressure, Screamer-Killers as fast T9 melee strikers, Tyrannofex for heavy-weapons reach, and Neurolictor for character sniping and objective disruption, this is an Invasion Fleet monster roster with the creature-feature weight of Crusher Stampede but the toolbox variety of a balanced all-comers list. The engine is maneuvering durable T9 bodies onto midfield objectives early while the Norn Emissary's ranged spike and Tyrannofex fire suppress the opponent's response, then grinding primary scoring through sheer wound-pool saturation across multiple 12"+ movement chassis. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists hard — Russ companies and static firing lines can't out-damage five T9+ frames before they close range, and blast templates lose efficiency against low-model-count monsters. Layered Lethal Combat lists and any build stacking AP-3+ Melta or concentrated anti-tank overload are the natural cracking tool, since all five anchor datasheets sit on the same toughness band and can be focus-fired off the table before the wound pool advantage ever materializes.

Tyranids.description: Built around paired Exocrines and Tyrannofexes as long-range fire platforms, backed by Termagant and Hormagaunt blobs screening forward objectives and Gargoyles providing mobile secondary coverage, this is an Invasion Fleet-style shooting list that weaponizes the Tyranid roster's unusual depth — a genuinely wide datasheet spread anchored by two of the faction's hardest-hitting ranged monsters. The plan is to plant the Exocrines and Tyrannofexes in second-row positions behind a wall of cheap bodies, grind primary scoring through sheer OC volume on the Termagant screen, and let the Maleceptor's psychic disruption protect the fire base while the guns delete whatever the opponent commits forward to contest. Against Heavy Gunline mirrors and Transport Infantry lists, the combination of blast-equivalent Bio-cannon volume, high wound pools on T10 Exocrine chassis, and expendable screening bodies makes the trade math heavily favorable — the opponent burns anti-tank resources on T10 monsters while Termagants quietly hold four objectives. The list cracks open against Mobile Anti-Armour Vehicles and fast melee lists that can close the gap before the fire base clears them: with no meaningful invuln saves on the shooting platforms and a 9.2 mobile-toolbox rating that doesn't actually translate into escape tools, a Knight list or deepstriking melee wave that reaches the Exocrines in turn 2 will gut the engine before it can pay off.

World Eaters.description: Built around Bloodletters, Flesh Hounds, Bloodcrushers, Skarbrand, and a Lord on Juggernaut backed by a Forgefiend, this is a Vessels of Wrath daemon-heavy swarm that floods the board with Khorne-marked bodies across multiple chassis types. The engine is a two-wave engagement: Flesh Hounds and Bloodcrushers close the mid-board on turn 1 while Skarbrand and the Juggernaut Lord threaten turn-2 pile-ins, with the Forgefiend providing AP-3 ranged cleanup on anything that tries to castle back. It punishes Mid-T Mixed Brawler lists hard — the daemon swarm's sheer activation count and Lethal Hits triggers on Bloodletter weapon profiles outpace War Horde's Sustained Hits 1 counter-punch when you're fielding comparable model volumes at higher toughness. Where it cracks is against Heavy Gunline Toolbox: Russ Demolisher cannons and Punisher salvos blast-template through the low-save Bloodletter core before the wave connects, and the Forgefiend alone can't threaten enough chassis simultaneously to suppress the firing line.
